post.description:
Server-sent events (`text/event-stream`), in this order:

1. `answer`, zero or more: `{text}`, a raw piece of the model's answer as it arrives. Replace it with `done.text` when the stream ends: long code is omitted in the final text.
2. Exactly one terminal event: `done` (the same payload as the JSON `TutorAnswerOut`), `unavailable` (`{code, note}`: the model did not answer), or `error` (a problem).

Refusals before the first event (no failing attempt, a refused endpoint) are JSON problems with the status of the JSON route.

post.summary: A hint at level 1-4: the reviewed text first, then the model's nudge

post.description:
Server-sent events (`text/event-stream`), in this order:

1. `reviewed`: the authored hint for the level, sent before any model call. Its payload is `{level, reviewed, hints_note}`. `reviewed` is null at L4 and when hints.md is missing.
2. `nudge`, zero or more: `{text}`, a raw piece of the model's answer as it arrives. It has not been through the output guards.
3. Exactly one terminal event:
   - `done`: the final answer, the same payload as the JSON `HintOut`. Replace the streamed nudge text with `done.nudge.text`, or clear it when `done.nudge` is null. Then `done.nudge_note` says why no nudge was given (held back, or the model answered nothing).
   - `unavailable`: `{code, note}`. The model did not answer; the reviewed hint stands.
   - `error`: an RFC 9457 problem with the domain `code`.

Refusals before the stream starts (unknown id, locked walkthrough) are JSON problems with the status of the JSON route, and no event is sent.
